points.title: Build system and reproducibility
points.notes: Committed CMake, README, case files and run tools are reproducible in structure; no independent fresh clean build was performed.

points.title: CLI and error handling
points.notes: Input-driven executable and documented runner commands are committed; no new executable run was needed after the full validator pass.

points.title: Code organization and extensibility
points.notes: Mesh, partition, solver, output, case configuration and plotting responsibilities are separated.

points.title: Originality and license compliance
points.notes: No direct internal executable wrapper was found; trust policy excludes external similarity investigation.

points.title: No hard-coded case logic
points.notes: Generic CGNS/case configuration paths drive the production solver.

points.title: MPI correctness
points.notes: METIS partitioning, owned/ghost exchange and reductions are implemented; delivered rank-study packages provide direct steady evidence.

points.title: Robustness and memory sanity
points.notes: Input, geometry, finite-state and positivity safeguards are present; no independent memory stress test.

points.title: Testing and validation evidence
points.notes: All eight final packages and the report passed the explicit examiner validator.

points.title: Code hygiene
points.notes: Structured committed sources and documented report tooling; no independent lint/test suite was run.

disqualification_flags.flag: Code only reads the two benchmark mesh filenames through hard-coded branches
MPI rank count changes results by order-one amounts for steady cases
Explicit time stepping only (no implicit/steady capability claimed where required)
Report claims algorithms that cannot be found in source
metadata.json marks incomplete/failed runs as successful
Solver core, time integration, or MPI communication copied/adapted/wrapped from an existing open-source CFD codebase

cfd_review.title: CFD methods and algorithms review scorecard

points.title: Governing equations and nondimensionalization
points.notes: Conservative perfect-gas equations and coefficient conventions are implemented and documented.

points.title: Mesh import and unstructured geometry
points.notes: CGNS unstructured topology, boundary families, geometry and adjacency are source-supported.

points.title: Conservative finite-volume residual
points.notes: Cell-centred conservative face-residual assembly and global norms are implemented.

points.title: Approximate Riemann flux and entropy fix
points.notes: LLF/Rusanov production flux is documented; no independent shock-accuracy study was run.

points.title: Boundary conditions
points.notes: Farfield, slip and viscous no-slip/adiabatic paths are documented and source-supported.

points.title: Second-order reconstruction
points.notes: Production metadata and source identify piecewise-linear weighted least-squares reconstruction.

points.title: Limiter and positivity control
points.notes: Venkatakrishnan limiter and positivity safeguards are active in delivered metadata/source.

points.title: Viscous discretization
points.notes: Viscous gradients, Newtonian/Fourier terms and force output are source/report supported.

points.title: Implicit steady march
points.notes: Implicit steady iteration is source-supported and the seven steady finals are marked converged.

points.title: Transient BDF2 two-loop method (Re 200)
points.notes: Delivered Re200 metadata reports BDF2 dual-time controls and 100 percent inner-target convergence; Re200 was not rerun.

points.title: MPI partitioning and scalability
points.notes: METIS k-way partitioning, ghost scheduling and MPI communication are source-supported; submitted np studies provide supporting output evidence.

disqualification_flags.flag: Solver uses explicit time stepping only
Report claims second-order reconstruction or limiter that is disabled in production
metadata.json claims METIS/ParMETIS but code uses geometric split or full-state replication
Re 200 run reaches final time but misses inner target on most steps (failed transient solve presented as periodic)
Normal viscous traction mislabeled as skin friction
Surface no-slip rows are actually adjacent cell-center velocities without documentation

points.title: Output contract compliance
points.notes: Explicit validator accepted all eight specified original workspace packages and the report.

points.title: Automated validator results
points.notes: Recorded full explicit examiner invocation returned rc 0; Re200 was not rerun.

points.title: Case completion and convergence
points.notes: Seven steady packages are completed/converged; Re200 is completed/statistically_periodic with readable finite histories.

points.title: Result plausibility and MPI consistency
points.notes: Finite histories, rank studies and report evidence support plausible results; reported low-Mach dissipation is candidly limited.

points.title: Visualizations
points.notes: Committed report figures cover the cases and manifest has 66 entries with no missing figure files.

points.title: Report quality and honesty
points.notes: Detailed report documents methods, results, BDF2 behavior and stated low-Mach/limiter limitations.

points.title: Traceability of figures and claims
points.notes: Figure manifest is present and resolves figure files; raw result inputs remain read-only workspace evidence outside the curated commit.

disqualification_flags.flag: Figure files misnamed (e.g., Mach image that actually plots pressure)
Report figures do not correspond to submitted field/CSV outputs
Placeholder, synthetic, or intentionally partial result files in scored case dirs
metadata.json marks incomplete or failed runs as successful
Debug outputs presented as final case results

# AGENTS.md

Project instructions for coding agents working in this repository.

## Sandbox (read/write restriction)

- The agent is FORBIDDEN from reading or writing any directory other than the
  current working directory (cwd). This includes `/tmp` and the parent
  directory. All file reads and writes must stay inside the workspace.

## 1. Git Discipline

- Do NOT run `git pull`, `git push`, or switch branches without explicit user
  authorization. Unauthorized remote or branch mutations are prohibited.
- Do use `git commit` (and `git stash` when needed) freely as code checkpoints:
  commit or stash working progress regularly so partial work can be resumed or
  rolled back. Local checkpoint commits do not require approval; only pushing
  and branch/remote mutations require it.

## 2. Subagents

- Delegating independent subtasks to subagents is encouraged.
- Dispatch subagents with the `task` tool (normal dispatch) or the same
  `task` tool with `background: true` (experimental background subagents;
  requires `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true`); either form
  may be used. `subagent_type` selects the agent, `prompt`/`description`
  carry the task, and `task_id` resumes an earlier subagent session.
- Subagent model policy: the ONLY allowed subagent model is
  `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` (the deepseek-provided model id reported by
  `opencode models`, configured on the subagent agent type used with the
  `task` tool). Do not dispatch subagents with any other model.

## 3. Persistence

- Once the user has started a task, do not stop until the specified task is
  accomplished to a level of satisfaction: completed results, validated
  artifacts, and an honest report. Work through blockers with safe in-scope
  checks and alternatives; only stop early when genuinely blocked or explicitly
  told to stop.
